territorial_scope.description: Florida state law that also reaches companion chatbot platforms and other AI firms outside the state that serve or do business with Florida users, by deeming them subject to Florida courts' jurisdiction.

evidence.quote: is therefore subject to the jurisdiction of the courts of this state

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: This bill text would amend Fla. Stat. s. 287.138 to bar governmental entities from knowingly contracting for AI technology with entities owned by, controlled by, or based in a foreign country of concern. It would create the Artificial Intelligence Bill of Rights (part IX of chapter 501), listing resident rights without creating new ones. Companion chatbot platforms would need parental consent for minor account holders, offer parents monitoring and time-limit controls, disclose AI status and remind minors hourly to take breaks. Bot operators must display hourly non-human notices, and AI technology companies may not sell or disclose personal information unless deidentified. The Department of Legal Affairs would enforce these as deceptive trade practices, with civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation and 45-day cure periods; minor account holders may recover damages of up to $10,000. The bill also amends s. 540.08 to require consent for commercial use of generative-AI likenesses and creates s. 1006.1495 limiting student access to AI instructional tools before grade 6 and requiring parental notice and opt-out. Effective July 1, 2026.

Stat. s. 287.138 to bar governmental entities from knowingly contracting for AI technology with entities owned by, controlled by, or based in a foreign country of concern. It would create the Artificial Intelligence Bill of Rights (part IX of chapter 501), listing resident rights without creating new ones. Companion chatbot platforms would need parental consent for minor account holders, offer parents monitoring and time-limit controls, disclose AI status and remind minors hourly to take breaks. Bot operators must display hourly non-human notices, and AI technology companies may not sell or disclose personal information unless deidentified. The Department of Legal Affairs would enforce these as deceptive trade practices, with civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation and 45-day cure periods; minor account holders may recover damages of up to $10,000. The bill also amends s. 540.08 to require consent for commercial use of generative-AI likenesses and creates s. 1006.1495 limiting student access to AI instructional tools before grade 6 and requiring parental notice and opt-out. Effective July 1, 2026.

notes: No legal_basis or implementing relation is stated; the department's rulemaking power in ss. 501.9984(8), 501.9985(5), 501.9986(6) is conferred by this text itself. Section 15 sets a July 1, 2026 effective date, but s. 287.138(3)(a) as amended begins restrictions on July 1, 2025, before that date. Section 2 directs the Division of Law Revision to create part IX of chapter 501; the new sections are created, not amended. Section 501.9985(3)(a) refers to a 'companion chatbot platform' in the operator cure provision, an apparent drafting inconsistency. The document has no bill number or version header, and the amended ss. 287.138 and 540.08 are not marked to show new versus restated text; the registry title refers to CS/SB 482. Internal references to s. 1006.1495 and to new ss. 501.9981-501.9987 are not coded as relations.
